solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mark items individually for lecture

definitions.meaning: to go down a list putting a check mark against each thing in turn
to scold or reprimand someone, as in a dressing-down

explanation.surface: A teacher marks each item on a list separately before giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: you check off a list item by item, and you rebuke someone when you give them a telling-off.

clue.text: 6 author put up

definitions.note: the answer to 6 down is a woven cloth made from flax; this fabric is a type of it

indicators.note: put up in a down light means the author's name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: George Eliot or T S Eliot, writers

explanation.surface: A writer is hoisted into place, referring back to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer at 6 down, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, often linen, cloth used for clothing and furnishing is an example of that fabric.

clue.text: John Thomas?

parts.note: a john is slang for a toilet, and Thomas was the first name of the Victorian plumber whose surname became slang for one

explanation.surface: A man's name, or a coy euphemism, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Crapper was a Victorian London sanitary engineer; 'john' is American slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for a lavatory, said to come from a Victorian plumber's surname.

clue.text: Gold top a third raised, one in four sections

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
the chest is the top part of the torso

indicators.note: a third of the six-letter word raised is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A gold peak lifted by a third, as if describing a section of a structure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third' takes the first third of RAISED, its opening two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony ensemble has four sections: strings, woodwind, brass and percussion, all playing together.

clue.text: Scottish area admitting book woeful with odd bits deleted, the other information

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the Scottish area holds the other pieces

parts.note: Fife is a council area and historic kingdom of Scotland
Acts is the book of the Bible after the gospels

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of woeful are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A Scottish region lets in a sorry book, minus odd parts, with some other news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with odd bits deleted' leaves OFL from WOEFUL. 'the other' is coy slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the euphemism for sex education, and 'the other' is British slang for sex.

clue.text: Darling animal put back in sack

indicators.note: in means the turned animal goes inside the sack word

parts.note: to hit the sack is to go to bed, so sack stands for a bed

indicators.note: putting back means the animal's name is turned round

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent

explanation.surface: Someone returns a pet creature to a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' is bed as in 'hit the sack', not a bag; 'put back' turns the rodent round before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a much-loved person, a synonym for one who is dearly cherished.

clue.text: Cake with tripe unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the nonsense word is cut off

parts.note: tripe is nonsense, also called bunk

explanation.surface: A dessert served with offal, not quite completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' means rubbish talk here, not offal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sweet bread roll, often iced, is a type of cake.

clue.text: Little boy getting in between sheets, perhaps

indicators.note: in goes between the letters of the boy's name, splitting it

parts.note: Len is the short form of Leonard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young lad climbs into bed between the bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boy in bed, but 'in' is just the two letters dropped into his short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed sheets are an example of household textiles made from flax.

clue.text: Girl clutching mountain plant

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the girl's name encloses the mountain

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A young woman grabs hold of a plant on a mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vervain, a garden flowering herb, is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Syrian mother has a part to play

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: A Syrian mother has been given a role in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part to play' is a division of a play, not an acting role.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to Damascus, the capital of Syria, so it describes something Syrian.

clue.text: Account added to tax-free plan, creating biblical figure

indicators.note: added to puts the account letters after the plan

parts.note: an ISA is a UK Individual Savings Account, a tax-free savings plan

explanation.surface: An extra account opened alongside a tax-free savings scheme yields a figure from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Abraham and Sarah in Genesis is a well-known Old Testament patriarch.

clue.text: Holy woman on business having something of a tattoo — that's a problem

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a nun is a woman in a religious order
a tattoo is a drumbeat, so a drum is part of what makes one

explanation.surface: A tattooed nun in commerce raises some puzzling questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tattoo' is not the ink on skin but a military drumbeat, as in the Edinburgh Military Tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or difficult dilemma is a synonym for a problem.

clue.text: Old jam, say

parts.note: EX means former, as in ex-wife
a press is a dense crowd, a crush or jam of people

explanation.surface: Some elderly preserve, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice or put into words is a synonym for saying something.

clue.text: Virgin son getting out more then?

parts.note: someone who gets out more stays in less, so this phrase gives the words in and less

explanation.surface: A sheltered lad is told that going out more would cure his inexperience.
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites the reading that a boy who gets out more is one who stays IN LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin here means pure or untainted, a synonym for being free of any wrongdoing.

clue.text: See 23
Plant maintaining resistance, it's felt

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the plant word keeps the letter inside it

parts.note: beet is a plant grown for its root
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A plant that keeps up its resistance is sensitive to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' is the fabric, not the past of feel.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft round flat cap is typically made of felt, so the hat is a thing that is felt.

clue.text: Maybe lead me into group in embrace of fertility god

indicators.note: in the embrace of means held inside the god's name

parts.note: Baal was a Canaanite fertility deity

indicators.note: into means the word me goes inside the group word

parts.note: a set is a group
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is drawn into a cult embraced by a pagan deity, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'into' works first inside the group word, then 'in embrace of' sets the result within the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is an example of a common non-precious metal, the opposite of gold or silver.

clue.text: Perfect cakes turned over inside burner

indicators.note: inside means the turned cakes go within the burner word

parts.note: a fire is something that burns

indicators.note: turned over means the cakes word is read backwards

parts.note: tarts are pastry cakes

explanation.surface: Flawless cakes were flipped while baking in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burner' is a fire, not a gas ring; 'turned over' makes the cakes read backwards before 'inside' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the highest class or quality is an idiomatic way to say excellent or perfect.

clue.text: Strip to get acting role?

definitions.meaning: to dismantle something into its pieces
read literally, to land a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone asks if undressing is the way to land a part in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismantling is a synonym for stripping down, and literally the words mean landing a role on stage.

clue.text: Ascertain when forced from an unorthodox group

indicators.note: forcing the word changes its shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Finding out under pressure about a breakaway faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when forced' rearranges the letters of ASCERTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a breakaway religious body, and this adjective describes belonging to one.

clue.text: Accommodate party, one enthralled by Brown

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a political party

indicators.note: enthralled by means captivated, held inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A political party member is captivated by Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was a Labour prime minister; here 'Brown' is just the colour, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold or have room for something is a synonym for accommodating it.

clue.text: Star like me, young one exploding

indicators.note: exploding blows the words apart so their letters land in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A youngster bursting onto the scene claims to be a celebrity like the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges LIKE ME YOUNG plus I into the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian pop singer and actress is a famous celebrity, a star of music charts.

clue.text: Bedraggled rat in queue for toilet

indicators.note: in means the rearranged rat goes inside the queue word

parts.note: a line of people is a queue

indicators.note: bedraggled means dishevelled, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A soaked rodent stands in line waiting to use the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedraggled' is the anagram signal for the rodent, and 'in' sets the jumbled letters inside the queue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A communal lavatory, as in a military camp, is a kind of toilet.

clue.text: See 18
Bird English composer sent skywards

indicators.note: sent skywards in a down light means the pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: An English composer is launched into the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English composer' splits: E for English, then BERG, who was Austrian.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird with lobed toes is a type of bird.

clue.text: Ate well, or didn't, drinking last of ale

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the fasting word holds the letter

parts.note: didn't eat well means went without food, i.e. fasted

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of ale

explanation.surface: Someone who either dined lavishly or went hungry while sipping beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't' stands for 'didn't eat well': went without food. 'drinking' puts E, from 'last of ale', inside FASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a lavish meal or banquet is to eat heartily.

clue.text: Singer lacking polish, bound to need discipline

parts.note: something not polished or cleaned is covered in dust
a bound is a leap, as is a spring
a field is a branch of study, a discipline

explanation.surface: An unrefined vocalist is sure to need some training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' is a jump, not tied up or certain.
explanation.definitionFit: The British pop vocalist of the 1960s, famous for Son of a Preacher Man, was a singer.

clue.text: Source of boiling water removing top from weed behind wood

indicators.note: behind means the weed piece comes after the wood

parts.note: teak is a hard timber

indicators.note: removing the top takes away the first letter of the weed word, its top in a down light

parts.note: a nettle is a stinging weed

explanation.surface: A gardener pulls the head off a weed growing behind the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing top from' drops the N of NETTLE, leaving ETTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot used for heating water for tea, so it is where boiling water comes from.

clue.text: Boob, a palindrome!

indicators.note: the clue says the answer reads the same either way, just as boob itself does

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation that a word for a breast reads the same backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the clue word and the answer read the same backwards; boob also means a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for a breast; boob also means a blunder, and the bird sense is a pun.

clue.text: Mistaken, alas, they say?

definitions.meaning: spoken, alas is 'a lass', and a lass is a miss, so 'a miss' is what alas says aloud

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over an error, quoting what others say.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition: spoken, 'alas' is 'a lass', which is A MISS; the question mark flags the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong or out of order is a synonym for being in error.

clue.text: Soft drug found in red jacket finally

indicators.note: found in means the drug letter sits within the red leader's name

parts.note: Lenin was the Soviet revolutionary, a Red
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of jacket

explanation.surface: Narcotics are discovered tucked into a crimson coat, prompting a mild reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' means a communist, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being soft on someone means being tolerant and merciful, not strict.

clue.text: Unsure when the reading, writing or arithmetic will come into homework?

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so these letters go inside the homework abbreviation

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is work on your own home
taken as written
each of these is one of the three Rs of basic schooling, so any one is an R

explanation.surface: A pupil wonders which basic school subject will feature in tonight's assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homework' means DIY, work around the house, not school work; the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant and indecisive, given to vacillating, is a synonym for being uncertain.
